_what: The quality / provenance columns appended to the 72-column corpus schema on 2026-10-30, taking it to 79. THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for their names and allowed values: build_dataset.py reads it to build the output header, every curation that emits a flag reads it to get the column names, and audit.py C13 reads it to enforce the vocabulary. Do not restate this list anywhere in code -- the reason these columns exist at all is that a per-curation flag was restated, drifted, and then silently died at the merge (review finding F-001).
_why: Before this, 1,137 corpus rows carried a convention rather than a measurement and said nothing about it. CLAUDE.md claimed the project flagged such rows 'in the data (positional_ambiguity, *_assumed, confidence)'; none of those columns existed, in data/ or in any file build_dataset.py's MERGE reads. The flags were produced, written into each curation's own QC JSON, and then dropped one stage BEFORE the merge, when each curation emitted the 72-column schema. So no change to the builder could have preserved them, and a consumer of data_vitro.csv could not tell a digitized colormap floor from a measurement.
_blank_means: not stated. It does NOT mean clean. A blank confidence on a curation that never assessed confidence is an absence of information, not an assurance -- which is why value_normalization_unit is populated for every row and the rest are not.

columns.name: Experiment_value_within_model
columns.meaning: Experiment_value re-standardized within (Experiment_ID x Model_type). Computed by build_dataset.py for every row whose experiment is on the z-score scale, by affine renormalization of Experiment_value -- which is exact, because a per-block z of an affine function of log10 signal is the per-block z of the signal. Identical to Experiment_value wherever an experiment has one Model_type. Use this where a between-assay offset would be a nuisance; use Experiment_value where it is the quantity of interest. Blank where the experiment is not on the z-score scale (the vivo blocks floored at 0). BLANK ALSO where the experiment's standardization block is not Model_type (F-080): re-standardizing inside Model_type there re-standardizes the union of blocks whose offsets are already deleted, and on ZH_2023 it returns a column byte-identical to Experiment_value on all 325 rows -- satisfying the letter of 'identical where an experiment has one Model_type' while defeating the purpose this column exists for. Corpus-wide this column does real work only for YX_2024, LZ_2025 and WT_2026; it is the identity on 41 of 43 vitro and 17 of 20 vivo experiments.

columns.name: value_normalization_unit
columns.meaning: The unit over which Experiment_value was standardized, stated on the row so a consumer never infers it. 'experiment' is the corpus convention (CLAUDE.md section 3). 'source_file' is WT_2026, where the authors' own dataset_info.txt forbids comparing across their seven files but their published Selectivity column compares cell types within one. 'experiment_x_model_type' is error class 22 -- the between-assay offset has been deleted -- and is only legitimate where that offset is unrecoverable from what we hold; see curation_note on those rows. 'experiment_x_model_target' is the same class of defect keyed on the ORGAN rather than the cell type (F-080): ZH_2023, BL_2023 and NG_2025_2 are standardized per Model_target upstream or by their own curation, and C12 could not see them because it partitioned on Model_type and no in-vivo experiment has more than one. For BL_2023 the token names ONE OF FIVE co-varying columns (Model_target, Route_of_administration, Dose_ug_nucleicacid, Dialysis_buffer, Mixing_method) -- the block is really the figure arm, and its curation_note says so. Note also that 'experiment' already means experiment-x-POOL for the nine experiments spanning data_vitro and data_vivo: each side sits independently at mean 0 / sd 1, so BL_2023's in-vitro rows are a third separately standardized block and say 'experiment'.

columns.name: confidence
columns.meaning: Confidence in the stored STRUCTURE, as assessed by the curation that produced it. 'low' means an element of the structure is an assumption the paper does not pin. Must be the lipid's own assessment: in ZT_2026 a join silently replaced it with the cholesterol-tail block's value under the same column name, turning 24 'low' rows into 'medium' and 'high' (F-011).

columns.name: positional_ambiguity
columns.meaning: 1 where which heteroatom bears which substituent is a convention rather than a measurement -- typically a one-pot library purified without chromatography, so the stored regiochemistry is one member of a mixture.

columns.name: structure_assumed
columns.meaning: 1 where a specific structural feature was assumed rather than read from the paper: a quaternization site the paper draws no structure for, a commercial reagent that is a branched isomer mixture sold under one name, an ester connectivity inferred from a single NMR shift. Pairs with curation_note, which must say WHICH feature.

columns.name: value_is_bound
columns.meaning: The value is a bound, not a measurement. 'upper' where the true value is at or below it -- a digitized heatmap cell on the colormap floor, where every value from 0 to the floor renders the same colour. 'lower' where the true value is at or above it -- a bar or point censored past the top of the axis. A model that treats these as measurements is fitting the floor of a colour ramp.

columns.name: curation_note
columns.meaning: One short sentence naming what is uncertain about THIS row and, where there is one, where the fuller account lives. Free text on purpose: a controlled vocabulary cannot carry 'two figures of the paper disagree 7.3x on this lipid' and a flag that cannot say what it means gets ignored. Written for a reader of data_vitro.csv who has not opened the curation folder.

columns.name: design_axis
columns.meaning: WHAT THE SCREEN ACTUALLY VARIED, so an analysis can exclude screens that carry no transferable chemistry without re-curating them. Derived at build time, not curated: 'formulation' where the experiment has exactly ONE distinct IL_SMILES (it measures formulation, dose or excipient effects on a fixed lipid and contributes no cross-source shared chemistry at all); 'mixed' where the ionizable lipid varies AND at least one lipid is measured at more than one formulation, so the two axes co-vary inside the experiment; 'chemistry' where the lipid varies and each lipid appears at one formulation. The within-lipid test is the point: a rule that called any formulation variation 'mixed' labelled YX_2024 -- 1,200 lipids at 2 formulations -- as mixed and would have dropped it from Result 3. Live counts: 49 chemistry (18,975 rows), 8 mixed (9,243), 6 formulation (2,780). Result 3 should use chemistry + mixed and report chemistry alone as a robustness check.

columns.name: lab
columns.meaning: THE LABORATORY, which Experiment_ID is not. Experiment_ID is a SCREEN key (INITIALS_YEAR of the FIRST author), and the project had been reading it as a laboratory key -- the manuscript title says 'Cross-laboratory prediction'. Derived mechanically by provenance/build_lab_map.py as the LAST AUTHOR of each paper's NCBI esummary record, which is the field's convention for the principal investigator. 54 experiments resolve to 22 distinct laboratories; Anderson DG alone holds 9. This column exists because of F-082: 79.1% of the in-vitro corpus's shared-lipid instances are WITHIN one laboratory, and the pair carrying 57% of Result 3's pooled points (AA_2008 <-> KW_2014) is Anderson <-> Anderson. Limits, which matter because this feeds a claim: last author is not always the corresponding author, co-senior authors collapse to one name, and scientific lineage is invisible (NC_2024 is Whitehead KA, first author of KW_2014 in Anderson's lab -- two labs by this rule, one tradition by any other). Read the same-lab/cross-lab split with that caveat stated.
